quizzes.stem: A review agent finished mapping a payments module on Monday. On Tuesday the team wants to compare a rewrite with a refactor from that same baseline, and the Monday thread must stay usable. What should the SDK call carry?

options.a: `resume` with the saved id and `fork_session` enabled
options.b: `continue_conversation` alone, which branches the latest run
options.c: `resume` with the saved id, once for each approach
options.d: A new run for each approach, opened with a summary of Monday

explanation.a: Fork is an option set together with a resume id, so it branches a copy and leaves the original usable.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "**Continue** finds the most recent session in the current directory", so it adds to that session and branches nothing.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Continue and resume both pick up an existing session and add to it", which puts both approaches into one history.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a summary carries only what was written down, and "whatever the summary leaves out is no longer in Claude's context", while a fork starts from a copy of the whole baseline.

quizzes.stem: A support service keeps one agent conversation per customer, all started from the same working directory. After a restart, each returning customer must get their own earlier conversation back. What does the service store for each customer?

options.a: A `continue` flag, set when their last run ended
options.b: A display name, passed to the SDK's `resume` option
options.c: The session id taken from their last result message
options.d: A fork of the first session, created for each customer

explanation.c: Resume needs a specific id, and the result carries it on every result.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Resume takes a specific session ID", not a display name; the guide's `--resume <session-name>` is a command-line form, and the SDK guide passes an id.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "**Continue** finds the most recent session in the current directory", and with every customer in one directory that is whichever conversation ran last.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Fork is different: it creates a new session that starts with a copy of the original's history", which is a second conversation and not a return to the first.

quizzes.stem: An agent mapped a service of twelve modules on Friday. Over the weekend a developer rewrote two of them. On Monday the team resumes the session. What should the first prompt add?

options.a: A request to survey the whole service from scratch
options.b: The paths of both edited files, to be read again
options.c: No addition, since the session already holds that analysis
options.d: The full text of both changed modules, pasted inline

explanation.b: Naming the differing files gives targeted re-analysis and keeps everything still true.
explanation.a: Ruled out because naming the files is "targeted re-analysis rather than requiring full re-exploration", and a survey discards what the resume kept.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Sessions persist the conversation, not the filesystem", so the weekend's edits are not in it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the notice "does not paste the new contents: the session reads them with its own tools".

quizzes.stem: Most of the files an agent analysed last month have since been rewritten, and its transcript is long. How should the next sitting start?

options.a: A new run that begins by pasting the earlier tool output
options.b: The full old transcript, with a line saying that things have changed
options.c: A fork of the transcript, so the original stays untouched
options.d: A new run that opens with a structured summary of the conclusions

explanation.d: When most results are stale, a summary of conclusions and their state is the reliable start.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a notice can correct a few files but cannot correct most of them: "More than half of the analysed files changed or are gone, or the session was idle for more than 7 days" is the course's rule for starting fresh.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a fork "creates a new session that starts with a copy of the original's history", stale results included.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a summary carries conclusions "never the raw tool output that went stale".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. The agent is built on the Claude Agent SDK and helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases and understand legacy systems. An engineer resumes a very large session on a Pro plan in Claude Code after a two-hour break. What should they expect from the first request?

options.a: A re-run of the session's tool calls, refreshing their results
options.b: A warm cache that still holds the earlier requests
options.c: A cache miss, with the full history processed once more
options.d: A cheap request, provided they choose the summary option

explanation.c: The prompt cache expires after a long pause, so the next request reads the history once more.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "after a long pause the prompt cache has expired, so the next request processes all of it again".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a resume restores the conversation and does not run tools again: a call that was cut off "doesn't finish or run again when you resume".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the expired cache means the next request "processes the full history once no matter which of the dialog's options you pick", the summary included.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. The agent is built on the Claude Agent SDK and helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases and understand legacy systems. A forked agent rewrote several modules in the shared working copy. The team wants that copy exactly as it stood before the run, and wants to keep the fork's conversation. What provides this?

options.a: Resuming the original session, which brings its files back
options.b: Deleting the fork's session so its edits are discarded
options.c: Forking again from the original, so the copy starts clean
options.d: Checkpointing, which snapshots the edits and reverts them

explanation.d: Only a snapshot of the files can return them to an earlier state.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Sessions persist the conversation, not the filesystem", so a resume restores no files.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "If a forked agent edits files, those changes are real and visible to any session working in the same directory", and removing the session does not undo them.
explanation.c: Ruled out because forking "branches the conversation history, not the filesystem", so the second copy meets the same edited files.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. The agent is built on the Claude Agent SDK and helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases and understand legacy systems. A service that follows this module's plan returns to saved sessions after nightly code changes. It records a digest for each analysed file and sees that 5 of 12 changed. What should it do?

options.a: Fork the session and keep the stale results in the original
options.b: Start a new session that opens with a structured summary
options.c: Continue the most recent session in the directory and add no note
options.d: Resume the session with a notice naming the five paths

explanation.d: Five of twelve is under half, so under the module's plan a resume with a notice naming the paths keeps what is still true.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a fresh start "keeps only what you decided was worth writing down", and five of twelve is under the half at which "a notice can correct a few files but cannot correct most of them".
explanation.c: Ruled out because continue takes the most recent session, and with no note the session believes the old files: "Sessions persist the conversation, not the filesystem".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a fork "creates a new session that starts with a copy of the original's history", stale results included.
